land.text: infobox 'Preceded by: Byzantine Empire; Kingdom of the Lombards': the Samnite lands of the southern Apennines on the Lombard-Byzantine frontier

predecessors.note: The page gives no boundary; the Eastern Roman Empire slug is the one that carries the Cliopatria Byzantine shape of 576 (its dossier is by eu-05). The Lombard side of the hand-over is the kingdom, whose Cliopatria row is Lombards (to 586) and then Kingdom of Italy.

land.text: 'little but the city remaining' when Guiscard returned the title to the papacy in 1081

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Papal States, Principality of Salerno, County of Apulia and Calabria'.

land.text: the principality's countryside and counties, held by Norman counts (the Norman page names Boiano, granted to Rudolf of Moulins, and Ariano), by the 1081 'little more than Benevento and its environs'

successors.note: The page names no Norman successor of the countryside beyond the infobox's County of Apulia and Calabria; the Norman Italy dossier (eu-13) should settle which parts.

capitals.name: Benevento
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Benevento'; the pages opened give no other seat, also under Atenulf I of Capua's union of 899-981.

keyframe_review.note: 35,922 km2 for 577..586. The page gives no area: 'Samnium: Paul the Deacon called the duchy the Samnite Duchy', Campania and Apulia are named as regions, Calabria and Salerno appear in the text. Infobox 'Established: 577'; the text gives 571 as the date some scholars propose (Zotto first duke, infobox 571-591), and says the Lombards 'may have entered later, around 590'.

correction.text: the 577 shape carried through 587-740: the 'Samnite Duchy' (Ducatum Samnitium), with Benevento as capital, in Campania and Apulia, under Lombard dukes (infobox 'vassal state of the Kingdom of the Lombards')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Benevento shape for 587..740 and draws the Lombard kingdom down to lat 39.7 over it. The page has the duchy ruled by its own dukes ('from 571 to 774'): Grimoald I, duke from 647, killed King Godepert and took Pavia in 662; in 663 Constans II besieged Benevento after landing at Taranto and Romuald I destroyed part of the Roman army at Forino; a peace with the Eastern Empire was signed in 680. The Kingdom of the Lombards page: 'the southern duchies were considerably more autonomous than the smaller northern duchies'. The growth of the shape from 35.9k (577) to 46.3k km2 (741) is not dated by any page opened; the 577 shape is the safe lower bound. Draw as a vassal tint of the Lombard kingdom.

46,296 km2 for 741..749. The Liutprand page calls Spoleto and Benevento 'independent southern Lombard duchies' about 741 and says Pope Zachary agreed to 'Liutprand's demand not to align with the dukes of Spoleto or Benevento'. The Duchy page names Capua and Crotone among Arechis's captures and lists the Byzantine holdings left afterwards (Naples, Amalfi, Gaeta, Sorrento, Calabria, the Apulian coastal cities Bari, Brindisi, Otranto), all undated; no infobox area.

correction.text: the 741 shape carried through 750-774, the duchy under its own dukes until Arechis II (infobox 758-774, 'last duke & first prince')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws the whole Lombard kingdom over Benevento for 750..774. The page: 'In 758 Desiderius briefly captured Spoleto and Benevento' (Principality of Benevento page agrees). The Kingdom of the Lombards page says the southern duchies 'were quick to ally themselves with the victors' after Aistulf's defeat.

46,656 km2 for 775..777. 774: after Charlemagne's conquest 'Arechis II took the title of princeps (prince)' rather than the royal dignity; the Kingdom of the Lombards page says Charlemagne 'never gained control of Benevento'. Principality page infobox: 'Sovereign state (774-787)'. No area given.

42,940 km2 for 778..787: the 775 shape loses a strip of about 3,700 km2 on the Abruzzo coast (lat 41.8-42.4, around Chieti). The Principality page says the Franks 'annexed Chieti to the duchy of Spoleto' in their attacks after 788, without a year; Cliopatria's 778 is kept at confidence 1. 787: forced by Charlemagne's siege of Salerno to submit to Frankish suzerainty (infobox 'Under Frankish suzerainty (787-1053)').

42,940 km2 for 793..839, the same shape as 778. 788: invaded by Byzantine troops led by Adelchis, repelled by Grimoald III with Frankish help; 814: Grimoald IV's vague promises of tribute and submission to Louis the Pious; before 839 Sicard imposed a tribute on Naples and captured Amalfi. The page's 'extent circa 851' map is after the partition. No infobox area.

24,066 km2 for 840..849: the western half of the old duchy has gone to Siconulf at Salerno (infobox 840-851; 'proclaimed prince in Salerno'), the formal division is dated 851 on the Salerno page and left undated (the ten-year war) on the Benevento page. Cliopatria's 840 is the de facto split. The page lists as Salerno's: Taranto, Cassano, Cosenza, Paestum, Conza, Potenza, Sarno, Cimitile, Capua, Teano, Sora; Cliopatria draws Capua as its own shape (840..865).

23,590 km2 for 850..874. The Principality page's map caption gives the extent 'circa 851': Benevento kept Molise and Apulia north to Taranto after the division; the Cliopatria shape agrees broadly. The page gives no area.
24,066 km2 for 875 only: cell-level difference from 850; the pages opened mention no change in 875.
23,590 km2 for 876..879. 876: the Byzantines retook Bari from the Saracens (Principality page), the first step of the Byzantine advance into Apulia.

12,882 km2 for 880..899: about 10,000 km2 of Apulia (east of lon 15.4) is gone. The Catepanate page: Bari under Byzantine control 'in 876', Otranto taken from the Saracens 873, 'mid-880s' expeditions of Nikephoros Phokas the Elder 'further extended Byzantine control over most of Apulia and Calabria', the theme of Longobardia established c. 892. Cliopatria's 880 is kept; the pages date the conquest only to the mid-880s. A Byzantine hold on Benevento itself in the 890s is not on any page opened.

correction.text: unchanged shape, 13,218 km2, but held from 899: 'In 899, Atenulf I of Capua conquered Benevento and united the two duchies'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: the page dates the union of Capua and Benevento to 899, Cliopatria's shape starts 900 and Cliopatria's Capua row ends 899. The shape (13,218 km2) is Benevento plus Capua's land. Lambert page: Lambert's rule 'was recognised in Benevento from 897'; he died in October 898.

correction.text: unchanged shape, 36,511 km2, but held from 967: Pandulf Ironhead 'ruled a large bloc of territories that stretched as far north as Tuscany and as far south as the Gulf of Taranto'; Otto I granted him 'the vacant Duchy of Spoleto and Camerino' in 967

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Benevento-Capua (13.2k km2) plus Spoleto (23.4k km2) is 36.6k, matching the shape. Pandulf was prince of Capua and Benevento from 943/944 (sole prince from 961), Spoleto and Camerino 967-981, Salerno 978-981; Benevento was made an archdiocese in 969.

correction.text: unchanged shape, 41,575 km2 (Benevento, Capua, Spoleto and Salerno), valid for 980 only: after Pandulf's death in March 981 the lands were partitioned among his sons

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria keeps the four-state bloc to 989, but the page has it partitioned at Pandulf's death in March 981 ('Landulf IV received Capua and Benevento. Pandulf II received Salerno') and Spoleto given to Thrasimund IV of Camerino by Otto II in 981. The Salerno shape is 5,063 km2, the Spoleto shape 23,388 km2: both are inside the 980 shape. See duchy-of-benevento_981.

correction.text: Benevento with Capua under Landulf IV, without Spoleto and Salerno: 'Landulf IV received Capua and Benevento'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 981..989 (13,218 km2, the 900 shape). Cliopatria keeps the 980 bloc to 989 and brings back a separate Capua shape only in 990.

12,882 km2 for 990..1009: Benevento without Capua. The Principality page: about 1000 Benevento 'still comprised 34 separate counties', and 'in 999 the Byzantines formed the Catapanate of Italy, further reducing Beneventan power' (the Catepanate page puts the catepanate at c. 965 and its first katepano in 970, a disagreement). No infobox area.
13,218 km2 for 1010..1014: the 900 shape (Benevento with Capua) comes back for five years. No page opened mentions 1010 or the 1015 end; Cliopatria's Capua row is absent in exactly these years.
12,882 km2 for 1015..1033. 1022: 'Henry II, Holy Roman Emperor conquered both Capua and Benevento' but withdrew after the failed siege of Troia (Principality page).

12,427 km2 for 1034..1039: the western edge moves from lon 13.40 to 13.87. The Norman page says nothing of Benevento in the 1030s; the strip coincides with Cliopatria's Capua shape of 1034 (960 km2, lon from 13.40). Norman Aversa is the neighbour.

12,234 km2 for 1040..1045. Principality page: 'The Prince of Salerno Guaimar IV took control of Benevento in 1040'; the Salerno page and the Norman page do not mention it. Norman page: 3 September 1041 the Normans defeated the catepan at Montepeloso and 'brought him to Benevento'; 1047 Henry III confirmed Aversa and demoted Guaimar to 'prince of Salerno'.

correction.text: the 1056 shape carried back through 1046-1055: Benevento and its countryside, from 1053 under papal suzerainty (infobox 'Under Papal suzerainty (1053-1081)'), Landulf VI prince from 1054

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Benevento shape for 1046..1055, and its Norman Italy shape of those years (24,721 km2, bbox 13.79..17.28 E, 40.48..42.11 N) covers Benevento's land. The pages opened do not show a Norman conquest of the principality: 18 June 1053 at Civitate the Normans captured Leo IX, 'imprisoning him in Benevento (which had surrendered)' (Norman page); the Principality page's own account of 1053 is garbled (Guiscard 'captured Benevento in 1053' and 'gave the city to Pope Leo IX'). The overlap with Norman Italy is for that dossier to arbitrate.
12,451 km2 for 1056..1065: papal-suzerain Benevento under Landulf VI (1054-1077, infobox) and minor Lombard dukes appointed by the popes (1053-1078).
12,234 km2 for 1066..1071: cell-level difference from 1056; the pages opened mention no change in 1066.

correction.text: unchanged shape, 12,234 km2, until 1080; in 1081 the principality ends with 'little more than Benevento and its environs'

keyframe_review.note: Years and extent: Cliopatria runs this shape to 1084, but the page ends the principality in 1081 ('Finally, in 1081 Guiscard returned the title to the papacy with little but the city remaining'); Norman page: 1077 the last Lombard prince died, 1078 the pope appointed Guiscard, June 1080 at Ceprano the pope gave Guiscard control of Benevento again, 1081 he relinquished it. From 1081 only the city and its environs remain, as papal land.

region.text: the 'Samnite Duchy' (Ducatum Samnitium), with Benevento as capital, in Campania and Apulia

ledger.note: 577: the Lombard duchy of Benevento under Zotto, 'Duke of Benevento'. Infobox 'Established: 577', capital Benevento; the text offers 571 as the date some scholars propose, and says the Lombards may have arrived later, about 590. The land is the page's regions, not a boundary.

region.text: the growth of the Samnite duchy between 577 and 741, toward Calabria and Apulia (Capua and Crotone among Arechis's captures, Taranto region)

ledger.note: 741: Cliopatria's shape has grown from 35.9k to 46.3k km2, eastwards and southwards. The page dates none of it: 'After Arechis, Byzantine holdings were reduced to Naples, Amalfi, Gaeta, Sorrento, Calabria, and the Apulian coastal cities'. Page silent on year; counterpart read from the Byzantine remnant it names.

region.text: Benevento, which King Desiderius briefly captured

ledger.note: 758: King Desiderius invades. 'In 758, King Desiderius briefly captured Spoleto and Benevento.' Counterpart is the Lombard kingdom, Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy row (587..774).

region.text: Benevento

ledger.note: 759: the duchies rise again. Duchy of Spoleto page: 'Spoleto and Benevento revolted while Desiderius was in the Roman Campagna'; the Benevento page says only 'briefly'. Year is the Spoleto page's.

774: after Charlemagne's conquest of the Lombard kingdom 'Arechis II took the title of princeps (prince)' instead of the royal dignity, and the duchy becomes the Principality of Benevento; infobox 'Established: 774', 'Sovereign state (774-787)'.

region.text: Chieti and the strip of the Abruzzo coast, annexed 'to the duchy of Spoleto'

ledger.note: 778: Cliopatria's shape loses about 3,700 km2 around Chieti. The Principality page says only that the Franks, attacking Benevento after 788, 'annexed Chieti to the duchy of Spoleto' (no year); the Spoleto page does not mention Chieti. Year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the western half of the old duchy, 'proclaimed prince in Salerno': Taranto, Cassano, Cosenza, Paestum, Conza, Potenza, Sarno, Cimitile, Teano and Sora (the 851 list; Capua too on the page, but Cliopatria draws Capua apart)

ledger.note: 840: Siconulf, freed by Amalfitan merchants after Radelchis seized Benevento on Sicard's murder in 839, is 'proclaimed prince in Salerno' (infobox 840-851) and holds the west. The land is the page's list as read onto Cliopatria's Salerno shape.

region.text: the civil war's ground: 'controlled mostly the western half of the old duchy'

ledger.note: 840-851: the decade-long civil war between Radelchis at Benevento and Siconulf at Salerno. The page has Lothair I's envoys, Guy I of Spoleto and Sergius I of Naples, mediating a division in 847; no campaign is dated.

region.text: the divided principality

ledger.note: 851: 'Louis, King of Italy, divided the principality into two sections' (Salerno page; the infobox says Emperor Louis II 'ends a civil war in Benevento by decreeing that the duchy be split into two distinct principates'). The Principality page leaves the division undated; the 849 date often given is not on either page.

region.text: most of Apulia: 'Byzantine control over most of Apulia and Calabria', after Bari (876) and Otranto (873)

ledger.note: 880: Cliopatria's shape drops about 10,000 km2 east of lon 15.4. The pages date Bari to 876 ('retook Bari from the Saracens', Principality page; 'passed under Byzantine control in 876', Catepanate page) and the wider advance only to the 'mid-880s'; the year 880 is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Capua, whose prince 'conquered Benevento and united the two duchies'

ledger.note: 899: 'In 899, Atenulf I of Capua conquered Benevento and united the two duchies.' The union is drawn under the Benevento row from 900 (13,218 km2); which side absorbed the other is the Capua dossier's to say. Lambert's rule had been recognised in Benevento from 897 (Lambert page); he died in October 898.

region.text: 'the vacant Duchy of Spoleto and Camerino'

ledger.note: 967: Otto I gives Pandulf Ironhead Spoleto and Camerino. 'Otto I granted Pandulf the vacant Duchy of Spoleto and Camerino.' The land is drawn from the Spoleto shape of 882, the last proper duchy shape; Cliopatria draws the union in the Benevento row from 970.

region.text: Salerno, where Pandulf 'succeeded as per their prior agreement'

ledger.note: 978: Salerno passes to Pandulf Ironhead. 'When Gisulf died childless in 977 or 978, Pandulf succeeded in Salerno as per their prior agreement.' The Salerno page dates Gisulf's death to 978 and says it 'passed into the wider realm of the Ironhead'; Cliopatria draws it in the Benevento row from 980.

region.text: Salerno, to Pandulf II

ledger.note: March 981: Pandulf Ironhead dies and his lands are partitioned. 'Pandulf's lands were partitioned among his sons': Landulf IV received Capua and Benevento, Pandulf II Salerno. The Salerno page says the Amalfitans then seized Salerno from Pandulf II.

region.text: Spoleto, 'given to Thrasimund IV'

ledger.note: 981: 'Otto II came down to Rome in 981, however, and Spoleto was given to Thrasimund IV,' duke of Camerino. Cliopatria keeps the Spoleto land in the Benevento row to 989. Reviewer eu-13-a: counterpart re-pointed from the person 'Thrasimund IV of Camerino' to holy-roman-empire, the emperor who disposed of Spoleto in 981 as Otto I did in the 967 gain.

region.text: Capua

ledger.note: 990: Cliopatria draws Capua apart again (384 km2) and Benevento shrinks to 12,882 km2. The pages opened are silent on any 990 event; the Salerno page says only that Capua 'made itself independent' under Guaifer, and that Guaimar IV later united his principality with Capua 'for the first time since Pandulf Ironhead'.

region.text: Capua

ledger.note: 1010-1014: Capua's land is in the Benevento shape again (13,218 km2) and Cliopatria's Capua row is absent. Page silent.

region.text: Capua

ledger.note: 1015: Capua returns as a separate shape. Page silent.

region.text: Benevento and Capua, 'conquered' by the emperor

ledger.note: 1022: Henry II's expedition. 'In 1022, Henry II, Holy Roman Emperor conquered both Capua and Benevento' but withdrew after the failed siege of Troia.

region.text: Benevento

ledger.note: 1022: the emperor withdraws after the failed siege of Troia; no separate date for the withdrawal.

region.text: the western edge of the Cliopatria shape, lon 13.40-13.87

ledger.note: 1034: Cliopatria's shape loses about 455 km2 on its western edge, where Cliopatria's Capua shape of 1034 reaches (lon 13.40). The Norman page is silent on the strip; the counterpart is read from the shapes.

region.text: Benevento, of which Guaimar IV 'took control'

ledger.note: 1040: 'The Prince of Salerno Guaimar IV took control of Benevento in 1040.' Only this page says so; the Salerno page (which has Guaimar extend his authority over Gaeta, Naples and Amalfi in 1038-1047) and the Norman page do not mention Benevento.

region.text: a sliver of about 190 km2 on the western edge

ledger.note: 1040: the western edge moves from lon 13.87 to 13.95, where Cliopatria's Norman Italy shape of 1040 (1,249 km2, from lon 13.40) lies. Page silent; counterpart read from the shapes.

region.text: Benevento

ledger.note: 1047: Henry III confirmed Aversa and Drogo as his vassal, 'Guaimar was demoted to prince of Salerno, and Capua went to Pandulf IV' (Norman page). The page does not say when Guaimar's hold on Benevento ended; 1047 is the bridging year.

1053: Benevento passes under the pope. Infobox 'Under Papal suzerainty (1053-1081)'; on 18 June 1053 at Civitate the Normans captured Leo IX, 'imprisoning him in Benevento (which had surrendered)'; the popes then appointed a series of minor Lombard dukes (Principality page). Used as a rename because the dossier and the colour continue; the overlord change belongs to the papal-states dossier. The two pages tell the Benevento events of 1051-1053 in different and partly contradictory words.
1078: 'Pope Gregory VII appointed Guiscard Prince of Benevento in 1078' (Landulf VI, last Lombard prince, died 1077; the infobox lists Robert Guiscard 1078-1081, 'last prince').

region.text: the city and its environs, 'little but the city remaining'

ledger.note: 1081: 'Finally, in 1081, Guiscard returned the title to the papacy with little but the city remaining.' The countryside is no longer Beneventan; the Norman page puts the principality at 'little more than Benevento and its environs' by then.

region.text: the Principality of Benevento

ledger.note: 1081: the Principality of Benevento ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 1081'); no prince is named afterwards. Cliopatria carries the shape to 1084.

wars.name: Constans II's expedition against Benevento
wars.outcome: Constans II landed at Taranto and besieged Benevento in 663; Duke Romuald I defended the city and destroyed part of the Roman army at Forino. A peace with the Eastern Empire was signed in 680.
wars.note: Before Cliopatria's 741 shape; no border is dated.

wars.name: Desiderius's capture of Benevento
wars.outcome: Desiderius 'briefly captured' Spoleto and Benevento in 758; both duchies rebelled in 759 while he was in the Roman Campagna.

wars.name: Frankish and Byzantine attacks on the principality

zones.text: Chieti, annexed to the duchy of Spoleto in the Frankish attacks after 788 (year not given)

wars.outcome: 787: Charlemagne's siege of Salerno forced Arechis II to submit to Frankish suzerainty. 788: Byzantine troops led by Adelchis invaded and Grimoald III repelled them with Frankish help. The Franks attacked Benevento several times and annexed Chieti to Spoleto. 814: Grimoald IV made vague promises of tribute to Louis the Pious.
wars.note: Only the 787 and 788 dates are the page's.

wars.name: Beneventan civil war

zones.text: the western half of the old duchy

wars.outcome: Radelchis (Benevento) and Siconulf (Salerno) fought for about ten years; Lothair I's mediators proposed a division in 847; Louis divided the principality in 851.
wars.note: The Principality page gives Sicard's murder as 839 and leaves the division undated; the Salerno page says 851.

wars.name: Byzantine reconquest of Apulia
wars.outcome: Bari passed to the Byzantines in 876, Otranto was taken in 873, and Nikephoros Phokas the Elder's expeditions of the mid-880s extended Byzantine control over most of Apulia and Calabria; the theme of Longobardia dates from c. 892.
wars.note: Benevento's side of these campaigns is not narrated on the page; the zone is read from Cliopatria's shapes.

wars.name: Pandulf Ironhead's war with the Byzantines
wars.outcome: Pandulf was captured at the Battle of Bovino in 969 and jailed in Constantinople; in 970 the Byzantines besieged Capua in his absence. No border moved.

wars.name: Henry II's expedition of 1022
wars.outcome: Henry II conquered both Capua and Benevento but withdrew after the failed siege of Troia.

wars.name: Norman conquest of southern Italy
wars.outcome: The Normans defeated the catepan at Montepeloso on 3 September 1041, captured Leo IX at Civitate on 18 June 1053 and held him in Benevento; the principality came under papal suzerainty in 1053, Robert Guiscard was its prince 1078-1081 and gave it back to the papacy in 1081.
wars.note: 1080 June at Ceprano the pope again gave Guiscard control of Benevento, to halt Norman incursions into the Abruzzi (Norman page).

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary line for the duchy or principality; the division of 851 and the partition of 981 are dated but their lines are only described by the cities listed. The 680 peace with the Eastern Empire pre-dates the first Cliopatria border after 587.

notes: Cliopatria's Duchy of Benevento row has 21 shapes (577..1084) with three gaps: 587..740 and 750..774, where the Lombard kingdom is drawn over Benevento, and 1046..1055, where Norman Italy's shape covers it. New keyframes carry the neighbouring shape through each gap at low confidence (the pages show the duchy under its own dukes or prince, not a boundary), so the map can draw Benevento as a vassal tint of the kingdom, then as a papal suzerain principality. 981..989 is a further new keyframe because Cliopatria keeps the 967-981 bloc (Benevento, Capua, Spoleto, Salerno) to 989 although the page partitions it in March 981. Overlord relations (Lombard, Frankish, imperial, papal suzerainty 787-1053-1081) belong to the overlords' dossiers as vassal events; here the changes of status are rename events (774 duke to prince, 1053 papal suzerainty, 1078 Guiscard). The Lombard kingdom 587-774 is Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy row, which the Kingdom of Italy part of eu-13 is to split; counterpart strings kingdom-of-italy stand for that Lombard half. Pages disagree: the division of the principality is 851 (Salerno page) or undated (Principality page); the Salerno page calls Capua part of Salerno's share while Cliopatria draws it apart; the Catepanate is c. 965/970 (Catepanate page) or 999 (Principality page); the Principality page's 1053 sentence has Guiscard capturing Benevento and giving it to Leo IX, which the Norman page does not support (Civitate, Humphrey, Leo IX held in a Benevento that had surrendered). Not on any page opened and so not recorded: the Byzantine hold on Benevento in the 890s, Guy IV's reign there (895), the 1015 and 1051 papal and imperial moves, Arechis I's conquests, Louis II's 866-871 stay, the Saracen emirate of Bari (847-871), Landulf's titles, the exact acquisitions between 577 and 741. The theme-of-Longobardia article (three titles tried) would not load. No page gives an area for the duchy or the principality, so the infobox check against Cliopatria's 12,000-46,000 km2 was not possible. The successor split in 1081 (city to the papal-states; the countryside to Norman counts) follows the Principality and Norman pages' 'little more than Benevento and its environs'. Page budget was 9; 10 pages were opened (the Spoleto page is cross-read for the 759 revolt).
